_comment: Places the Bologna (SBN-UBO) records, which carry no Milan shelfmark, on a bookcase of eco-video/layout.json from their subject data.
Rules are tried in order; the first that matches wins. A rule matches when any `dewey` prefix matches one of the record's Dewey numbers,
or any `keywords` regex (case-insensitive, accents folded) matches the record's subjects, dewey labels, series or title,
or `author` matches the main author (700 field). `bookcase` is one id or a list; with a list the records are dealt across the
bookcases in order (round-robin by hash of the id, so a rerun places the same book on the same bay).
Records that match no rule go to `fallback` with placement_note 'no subject match' and are counted in meta.counts.placement_unknown.
Fondazione captions per bookcase are in layout.json (subject field). Edit freely: this file is data, the generator only reads it.
Matching is done on fold()ed text: accents are stripped and everything is lower-cased, so write keywords without accents (esthetiq, not esthétique).
SBN titles carry a '*' non-filing marker after the article (Il *libro): write `il \*?libro`, not `il libro`.
`confidence` (high = the Fondazione caption of the target bookcase names the subject, medium = nearest defensible bay) and `note` are documentation; the generator ignores them.
Order: the two Eco rules, then specific author / named-work / series rules, then the broad Dewey + keyword rules per bookcase, then generic single-word rules that only
records nothing else matched can reach. Journals and volumes catalogued with only a volume number as title (their set title is in UNIMARC 461, which the generator does not read) stay on the fallback.

A rule may carry `subjects` (regexes matched on the record's subject headings only, folded like the keywords), tried after `author`, `dewey` and `publisher` and before `keywords`; five '(subject heading)' rules for the national literatures stand before the generic subject rules, so a novel whose heading says 'Narrativa italiana' is never shelved by a word of its title.
`subjects`: regexes read on the record's subject headings and Dewey labels alone, never on the title or series, tried after `dewey` and `publisher` and before `keywords`.
